name: Tawang Monastery (Gaden Namgyal Lhatse)
description: Largest Buddhist monastery in India and second-largest in the world, founded in 1680-81 by Merak Lama Lodre Gyatso under the guidance of the 5th Dalai Lama. Perched at about 3,000 m overlooking the Tawang Chu valley, it belongs to the Gelug school and houses a large golden Buddha statue, rare manuscripts, and around 450 monks.
facts: Founded 1680-81 by Merak Lama Lodre Gyatso
Largest monastery in India; second-largest worldwide
Houses ~450 monks and rare Kangyur/Tengyur manuscripts
Birthplace region of the 6th Dalai Lama nearby

name: Sela Pass
description: High-altitude mountain pass at about 4,170 m (13,700 ft) on the border of Tawang and West Kameng districts. Gateway to Tawang on NH-13, surrounded by snow-capped peaks, with the sacred Sela Lake nearby that often freezes in winter. Named after a local Monpa girl in legend.
facts: Connects Tawang to Dirang and the rest of India
Sela Lake at ~4,160 m freezes in winter
Border between Tawang and West Kameng districts
Sela Tunnel provides all-weather connectivity below the pass

name: Sangetsar Tso (Madhuri Lake / Shonga-tser Lake)
description: High-altitude glacial lake at about 3,708 m on the road to Bum La Pass, formed by an earthquake that submerged a forest, leaving dead tree trunks standing in the water. Popularly known as Madhuri Lake after a Bollywood song sequence was filmed here.
facts: About 35 km north of Tawang town
Formed by earthquake; dead trees remain in the water
Named Madhuri Lake after film Koyla shoot
Army permit often required along Bum La road

name: Nuranang Falls (Jang Falls / Bong Bong Falls)
description: 100 m high curtain waterfall near Jang town, about 2 km northeast of Jang and 40 km from Tawang. Fed by the Nuranang Chu originating from Sela Pass slopes; features a small hydel plant at the base. Popular stop on the way to Tawang.
facts: Also known as Jang Falls or Bong Bong Falls
About 40 km from Tawang near Jang
Small hydel plant generates local electricity
Song from film Koyla filmed nearby

name: Bum La Pass
description: High-altitude border pass at about 4,600 m (15,200 ft) on the India-China frontier, about 37 km from Tawang. Historic trade route and site of intense fighting in the 1962 Sino-Indian War; Border Personnel Meeting point. Requires special Army permit.
facts: Special Army/DC permit required; Indian nationals only

name: Urgelling Monastery (Ugyenling)
description: Historic Buddhist monastery about 3 km from Tawang town, birthplace of the 6th Dalai Lama Tsangyang Gyatso in 1683. Founded in the late 15th century; smaller and quieter than Tawang Monastery, belonging to the Nyingma tradition.
facts: Smaller and less crowded than Tawang Monastery

name: Jaswant Garh War Memorial
description: Memorial near Nuranang/Jang dedicated to Rifleman Jaswant Singh Rawat of 4 Garhwal Rifles, who fought heroically in the 1962 Sino-Indian War and was awarded the Maha Vir Chakra posthumously. Maintained by the Indian Army with daily rituals as if he were still serving.
facts: Honours Rifleman Jaswant Singh Rawat, MVC (posthumous)
Located near Jang/Nuranang, about 25-40 km from Tawang
Site of Battle of Nuranang in 1962

name: Gorsam Chorten
description: Large ancient Buddhist stupa near Zemithang, about 90 km from Tawang, modelled after Boudhanath in Nepal. Believed built in the 12th-14th century by a local Monpa lama; features prayer wheels and is a major pilgrimage site.
facts: About 90 km west of Tawang near Zemithang
Modelled on Boudhanath Stupa of Kathmandu

name: Zemithang (Pangchen)
description: Remote border village and circle headquarters on the Nyamjang Chu river, about 85-90 km from Tawang near the Bhutan and Tibet borders. Entry point for the 14th Dalai Lama into India in 1959; home to Gorsam Chorten and black-necked crane wintering habitat.
facts: First Indian village entered by 14th Dalai Lama in 1959

name: Tawang War Memorial
description: 40-foot-high stupa-style memorial near Tawang town commemorating the Indian soldiers who died in the 1962 Sino-Indian War. Features names of the fallen and overlooks the Tawang valley; daily bugle ceremony held by the Army.
facts: About 2 km from Tawang town centre
Scenic overlook of Tawang Chu valley

name: Pankang Teng Tso (PT Tso / Panga Teng Tso)
description: High-altitude glacial lake at about 3,900-4,000 m on the road toward Bum La Pass, about 17-18 km from Tawang. Quieter alternative to Madhuri Lake with mirror-like reflections of snow peaks; sacred to local Monpa community.
facts: On the route to Bum La Pass

name: Tawang Town
description: District headquarters and main tourist base at about 3,000 m elevation, named after the famous monastery. Gateway for exploring the region’s monasteries, lakes, passes, and Monpa culture; requires Inner Line Permit.
facts: Main base for Tawang tourism circuit
Inner Line Permit required for entry
